newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volksfuersorge units plan capital increases.
newsitem.headline: Volksfuersorge units plan capital increases.

text.p: German insurer Volksfuersorge Holding AG said on Thursday that both its life and non-life subsidiaries planned multi-million mark capital increases.

Volksfuersorge's non-life subsidiary, Volksfuersorge Deutsche Sachversicherung, plans a 140 million marks ($83 million) capital increase, while its life insurance unit Volksfuersorge Deutsche Lebenversicherung plans to raise nominal capital by 20 million marks to 220 million marks.
In a compulsory statement, the group said both its life and non-life units planned to raise their respective dividends to 12.50 marks per share for 1996 from 12 marks a year ago.
The group decided at its annual shareholders meeting to raise capital in the non-life group by 14 million to 154 million marks using a cash injection of 140 million marks.
The capital raise in its life group would involve an increase of 20 million to 220 million marks, using a cash injection of 200 million marks.

The capital raise will involve the issue of 280,000 new shares at 50 marks each in its non-life unit, while its life unit capital raise will involve the issue of 400,000 new nominal shares at 50 marks each.
The new shares in the non-life unit will be issued to shareholders on a 10 to one basis, based on their current shareholdings, at a price of 75 marks per share.
Shares in the new life unit will be issued to shareholders at a price of 75 marks per share.
In both capital raises, shareholders will be entitled to retroactive earnings from January 1, 1997.
Volksfuersorge Holding is majority-owned by Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs-Aktiengesellschaft AG .

Volksfuersorge Deutsche Lebensversicherung achieved an 11 percent rise in gross earnings to 1.26 billion marks last year, while Volksfuersorge Deutsche Sachversicherung AG reported unchanged premium income of 1.19 billion marks last year due to a decline in premiums for motor vehicle insurance. ($ = 1.686 German Marks)
